Decided 2026-11-22: all recommendations accepted; stage 1 started.

cl_kit: one platform for cl_audit and cl_quick

The shared Swift library behind both Mac apps, and how to make both apps answer "which account is this folder on, and whose numbers are these" the same way. Read-only audit of cl_kit 26.11.3 (both apps vendor it; cl_kit main has nothing newer) and of both apps' sources, 2026-11-22. Sample addresses only.

Short answer.

Not finished. Today only two things are truly shared by both apps: hiding addresses on screen, and the Claude Code sign-in in a Terminal window. The kit already holds a correct "which account is the folder on" rule, where a running claude's own word beats the .claude.json file, but neither app calls it. cl_audit decides with its own reader and resolver, cl_quick with its own copies, and on the same folder they can disagree in 5 places.

The target: each question gets one answer, written once in the kit and asked by both apps. The apps only draw the answer. First the account rule, with the 5 disagreements settled by you below. Then cl_quick moves onto the kit's usage rules and runner, and cl_audit onto the shared status record. What only one app needs (cl_audit's session-move switch, the Claude window, cl_quick's chat views) stays in that app.

2 · Design rules

1One question, one answer, in the kit"Which account is the folder on", "whose numbers are these", "is it full", "is it stale" each have one function in cl_kit. No app computes them again.
2Apps only drawAn app passes in what it read and gets back a value to show: the account, a tick, the numbers or why there are none. Colours, fonts and words stay in the app.
3Numbers belong to the source that gave themA running claude's numbers belong to its own initialize account; numbers read with a Keychain sign-in belong to Anthropic's reply for that sign-in. The .claude.json file is only a guess.
4Two questions get two names"Claude Code's account" and "the Claude window's account" are different questions. The kit answers the first; cl_audit answers the second, and never calls either one plainly "in use".
5What only one app needs stays in itThe session-move switch, the flow lock, the Claude window and the Keychain path stay in cl_audit. The chat views stay in cl_quick. The kit grows only by jobs both apps do.
6The kit's layers stay cleanProfileCore, then Runs, then ClaudeAuth: Foundation only, no app paths, words or global state, and no logging. AddressPrivacy, and any shared view module, stands apart.
Rules both apps keep through the move
  • cl_quick never reads the Keychain or any token (the kit's no-Keychain build). Its usage comes only from a short-lived claude asked for its usage, with no model message.
  • One Claude Code folder per profile, never extra or hidden folders per account. Standby accounts are never read.
  • cl_quick stays fully incognito: nothing about chats on disk, only its levels file and settings.
  • In cl_quick, the running claude's word comes from the chat's own process and from the usage refresher. Neither ever runs in a standby account's folder, and the refresher asks only when the numbers are older than 5 minutes.
  • The account in use is ticked, with no "· in use" text. Never a bare name cut from an address.
  • A hidden address is the kit's one fixed stand-in or "hidden address", never the real text blurred or masked.
  • A week-only account shows no 5-hour row anywhere: hidden only when the account has a week and has never had a 5-hour number. An old 5-hour number is never dropped, because an idle 5-hour account's usage answer also has no 5-hour number. Stale is never "full". "Week" is the seven-day limit.
  • Checks never touch the operator's screen, keyboard or clipboard.

4 · The account rule, settled point by point

Each point is your decision; reply with the words in blue. The recommendation is marked green. Samples: wu@example.com with a personal plan and a Team seat; zedekiah@example.com.

D1What counts as "signed in"

The file names an account by its id, its address, or both. A running claude names it by address and organisation name only, never by id.

A1 idSigned in only when the file has an account id (cl_audit today). A process's word could then never count on its own.
A1 addressSigned in only when there is an address (cl_quick today). A file with an id and no address reads as signed out.
A1 eitherSigned in when the id or the address names someone (the kit's rule today). A saved key still needs the id: until it comes, an address placeholder stands in and is upgraded once the id appears.

Why either: it is the only choice that lets a running claude's word count, and it is already what the kit does. The saved-key rule keeps cl_audit's stored seats exact and is how cl_quick's email: placeholders already work.

D2Personal and Team seats on one address

wu@example.com can have a personal plan and a Team seat. They share the address and even the account id; only the organisation tells them apart, and each has its own limits.

A2 apartTwo seats: by organisation id when both sides know it, else by organisation name. When only one side names an organisation, the answer is "same address, seat not known", and no plan or ids are borrowed from the file.
A2 sameOne account per address (cl_quick today). Simpler, but a Team seat's numbers can show on the personal plan and the other way round.

Why apart: the numbers really differ between the two seats, and the running claude says its organisation, so cl_quick can tell them apart too. This also merges the kit's two seat comparisons into one.

Cost for cl_quick: it keys its accounts and levels by account id only, so today both seats share one entry. The move:
  • The organisation id becomes an added field on the account entry; the identity is (account id, organisation).
  • An entry with no organisation is "seat not known", upgraded in place when the organisation is first seen, the way email: placeholders are upgraded to the account id today.
  • Numbers are never copied onto both seats.
  • The levels file's keys profile|uuid become profile|uuid|org. An older build reads the new key as a miss: harmless, it shows no numbers until its next usage ask.

D3A running claude's word

Claude Code writes .claude.json when a sign-in lands; a claude that is already running keeps the account it started on. Between the two, the file and the process disagree.

A3 processThe process's own initialize account wins over the file, which is only a guess. Anthropic's reply for cl_audit's Keychain sign-in counts as the same kind of verified word. When they disagree, the answer says "differs" and numbers are kept only for the verified account.
A3 fileThe file wins (cl_audit today). Simpler, but numbers can be put on an account the process isn't on, just after a sign-in elsewhere.

Why process: it is the standing rule (usage belongs to the running process's own initialize account), cl_quick already works this way and its hub wants it to win, and the kit's rule already does it. It also takes two of the kit's open gaps from cl_quick: an organisation renamed while the process runs keeps its numbers when the organisation id is the one it started on, and a process that said nothing is trusted only while the file is unchanged since its launch.

What it costs cl_audit, and how it fits its Keychain path.
  • cl_audit's numbers come from the usage API with the Keychain sign-in; Anthropic's reply names that sign-in's account. That reply is already a verified word in the kit, so nothing changes in how it reads numbers. The rule simply becomes the kit's: verified word over file.
  • cl_audit must also ask the process, which it never does today. A short claude (start, read initialize, stop; no model message) costs a second or two and a Node process each time. So it asks only when the sign-in changes or the file and Anthropic's reply disagree, never on every 3-second tick, and only in the profile's own folder, never a standby account.
  • Its quick chat already runs claude: that process's word is used for free while it runs.

D4A profile with a Claude window

In cl_audit, a profile can own a Claude window (the desktop app) as well as a Claude Code folder, and the two can be signed in to different accounts. cl_quick only knows Claude Code.

A4 two namesName the two questions apart. "Claude Code's account" is the kit's answer, the same in both apps. "The Claude window's account" is cl_audit's own answer. Each row ticks the account for its own question; when the two differ, cl_audit says so in one labelled line.
A4 code"In use" means Claude Code's account everywhere; the Claude window's account becomes a note under it.
A4 windowThe kit learns the Claude window too. This breaks rule 5: cl_quick would carry a concept it never uses.

Why two names: they are two real questions with two real answers, and forcing one hides the split that cl_audit's B8 fix (the Claude app and Claude Code on different accounts) exists to show. cl_quick and cl_audit then agree on every Claude Code answer, and only cl_audit adds the second.

D5Organisation names

A5 ignore caseThe organisation id decides when both sides have one; else the name, ignoring case (the kit today).
A5 exactNames must match exactly (cl_quick today). A change of case alone would cut a running chat's numbers.

Why ignore case: ids decide wherever they exist, and a running claude gives only the name. Two organisations whose names differ only in case on one address is not a real case.

5 · Stages across both apps

Each stage is a small release. Delivery for every stage, as both Mac apps run it since 2026-11-21: compile and install per change, no suites per change; reviewers read the diff only; CI on push is an early warning, and its reds are fixed in one batch before the release; the full suites run only at release. Every stage that changes how an app looks also updates that app's site in the same release.

Kit laneStages 1, 5 and 8's module, one kit release each. Kit work in different folders (Auth, Core, Run) can overlap.
cl_quick laneStages 2, 6, then 10. Stage 2, then 6, never overlapping: both touch the menu's usage file (MenuUsage.swift), and so does stage 8. The no-5-hour branch has landed (33f2818), so nothing waits on it.
cl_audit laneStages 3, 4, 7, then 9. Stage 7 (status record) is file-disjoint from 3 and 4.

6 · Risks to watch

A sign-in under a running claudeThe file names the new account before the process stops. The rule must answer "differs" and drop numbers for the account the process isn't on, in both apps, never moving them to the new account.
Team seatsOne address and one account id, two seats. Any place that still compares by address or id alone will mix their numbers. The checks need a personal-plus-Team sample in every suite that matches accounts.
cl_quick's stored keysprofiles.json keys accounts by account id, or by an email:<address> placeholder when the file had none, and its levels follow. The organisation is an added field on the entry, an entry without one is "seat not known" and is upgraded in place, and numbers are never copied onto both seats. Keep a backup before the first upgrade.
A downgrade after two seatsAn older cl_quick treats the account id alone as the identity (Accounts.swift:243). After a downgrade from a state with two seats on one address, it shows one row for both, and its levels keys miss until its next usage ask.
The Keychain stays out of cl_quickNew kit code in ClaudeAuth must not reach the Keychain from a shared path. The kit's no-Keychain build check runs on every kit release, and cl_quick's build leaves the Keychain file out.
The short ask in cl_auditRuns claude in the profile's folder: only that one folder, never a standby account, no model message, nothing written about chats, and a timeout. Asked on change, not on every tick.
Two kit versions in the fieldUntil both apps ship on kit 26.11.4, they can still disagree. Ship stages 2 and 3 close together. Older cl_audit Dock icons still read status records, so record changes only add fields.
The week-only rule movingIt landed in cl_quick on 2026-11-22 (33f2818). Moved into the kit, it must keep its exact form: never drop an old 5-hour number, since an idle 5-hour account's usage answer also has none. In cl_audit it is new behaviour, so its checks and site change with it.
Checks off the operator's machine stateEvery new kit and app check stays headless: no screen, keyboard or clipboard, no real addresses, no reads of real .claude.json, account lists or the Keychain.

7 · The two product decisions

Finding accounts on the Mac (item 7)

discovery kitThe kit holds each source as a plain function; each app picks its sources. cl_audit keeps all of them; cl_quick adds the profile folders' own files and backups, never transcripts (it stays incognito and never reads chats).
discovery appLeave it as today: cl_audit finds every account, cl_quick lists those it has seen signed in. Two lists can show different accounts.

Why: one way to read each source, without forcing cl_quick to read what it shouldn't. Small to medium.

Quick chat (item 8)

chat oneOne copy, cl_quick's (the cl_quick hub's view). cl_audit's chat item opens cl_quick on that profile and keeps no chat of its own. The chat views stay out of the kit; only the account and usage rules go in (folder reader, process trail, full and stale, time words).
chat twoKeep both copies, each on the kit's rules. No new dependency, but two chats to keep in step, about 2.7k lines in cl_audit.

Trade-off: with chat one, cl_audit's quick chat works only when cl_quick is installed. Without it, cl_audit shows the chat item with "Get cl_quick" in its place. With chat two, every chat fix is done twice.
